title: Marguerite and the Garden
premise: Ulyana Winterbourne carves bones into charms that let the valley's dead speak, in a place where magic cannot follow — until a boy named Marguerite arrives at her door speaking a language older than any kingdom, carrying a seed from the Garden, the vanished country that once held all magic. The Garden is falling into an endless winter, and its last door can only be opened by someone who hears the dead. To save the boy, Ulyana must leave the valley that exiled her, confront the truth that she was cast out for betraying the Garden's queen, and choose between loyalty to the people who sheltered her and the truth of what she did. In the end she opens the door with her own confession carved into bone, sends Marguerite home to a spring-returning Garden, and remains behind as the valley's keeper of both its living and its dead.
about_author: Xanthe Vasquez is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing funeral customs across three continents before turning to fiction. They write quiet, wintry fantasy about grief, exile, and the small mercies people trade for survival.

chapters.title: The Valley Where Magic Cannot Follow
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. We meet the bone-carver at work, listening to the valley's dead through carved charms, bound by a law she barely questions: no magic crosses the ridge. Emotional beat: contentment built on forgetting.

chapters.title: A Knock in the First Snow
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. A boy arrives half-frozen, speaking a language no one knows — yet Ulyana understands it, and the dead in her workshop stir for the first time in years. Emotional beat: dread disguised as curiosity.

chapters.title: The Boy Called Marguerite
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. He remembers a garden, a queen, and a winter that never ends, but not how he crossed the ridge. Ulyana hides him from neighbors already asking questions. Emotional beat: fragile trust between strangers.

chapters.title: What the Bones Remember
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. A carved charm speaks a name Ulyana buried long ago: her own, spoken by the Garden's dead queen. She realizes the valley's silence was arranged — by her. Emotional beat: vertigo of self-betrayal discovered.

chapters.title: The Reeve's Questions
chapters.summary: Village reeve Halvard's POV. Strangers have come asking after a child; Halvard, who loves Ulyana quietly, deflects them but begins his own inquiry. Emotional beat: loyalty tested by duty.

chapters.title: Lessons in a Dead Tongue
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. He teaches Ulyana fragments of the old language; each word she speaks makes the valley's wards flicker. Emotional beat: wonder curdling into guilt.

chapters.title: The Queen's Confession, Half-Carved
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. Flashback woven through present: decades ago she served the Garden's queen and traded the Garden's location to save her own life during the purge. Emotional beat: shame she has never said aloud.

chapters.title: Hunters at the Ford
chapters.summary: Halvard's POV. The strangers are revealed as the Wardens who ended magic's age, still hunting Garden remnants. Halvard lies to them and knows it will cost him. Emotional beat: fear sharpening into resolve.

chapters.title: The Seed in the Boy's Chest
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. She discovers Marguerite carries the Garden's last living seed; if he dies, the country dies truly. The Wardens want him; so, she realizes, does the winter itself. Emotional beat: protective love with a deadline.

chapters.title: Doors That No Longer Exist
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. He describes the way home: a door that opens only for a confession the Garden accepts. Ulyana says nothing about what hers would cost. Emotional beat: hope shadowed by concealment.

chapters.title: Firelight Politics
chapters.summary: Halvard's POV. The village debates sheltering the boy; old grievances surface, including whispers about why Ulyana came here. Emotional beat: community fracturing under pressure.

chapters.title: The Warden's Offer
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. A Warden finds her alone and offers absolution: give up the boy, and her exile ends, her past erased. Emotional beat: temptation dressed as mercy.

chapters.title: Midwinter Vigil
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs braided. The longest night; the dead grow loud, the wards fail at the edges, and the first true cold of the falling winter touches the valley. Emotional beat: collective holding of breath.

chapters.title: Betrayal in Bone
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. He finds Ulyana's old confession-charm hidden in her workshop and learns she betrayed the Garden. He flees into the snow. Emotional beat: heartbreak of a child learning adults lie to survive.

chapters.title: The Long Fall
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. She searches the blinding storm, pursued by Wardens and haunted by every voice she ever silenced. Emotional beat: penance begun in motion.

chapters.title: What Halvard Knew
chapters.summary: Halvard's POV. He reveals he has always known who she was and chose her anyway — then takes a Warden's blade meant for her. Emotional beat: love proven at terrible price.

chapters.title: The Door Beneath the Ice
chapters.summary: Ulyana and Marguerite's shared POV. Following the dead queen's voice, they reach the buried threshold of the Garden, where the winter waits like a patient animal. Emotional beat: awe and terror entwined.

chapters.title: Confession Carved in Living Bone
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. At the door she carves her full confession — name, betrayal, cowardice — into her own arm's bone and speaks it in the dead tongue. The door recognizes the cost. Emotional beat: catharsis through self-destruction.

chapters.title: The Queen's Judgment
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. Within the threshold, the dead queen meets them; she asks not for punishment but for witness. Ulyana's truth, freely told, is the first thing the Garden has accepted in a century. Emotional beat: forgiveness that does not erase.

chapters.title: Spring Behind the Door
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. The seed is planted; the Garden's winter breaks at its edges. The door will close forever once he passes through. Emotional beat: bittersweet farewell between the boy and the woman who saved him.

chapters.title: The Keeper of Both
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. She returns to the valley as the Wardens withdraw, magic's age ending not in conquest but in a garden going home. She buries Halvard beneath the ridge where the wards once stood. Emotional beat: grief transmuted into vocation.

chapters.title: Marguerite and the Garden
chapters.summary: Coda, Marguerite's POV years later. In a green country he carves a bone charm in Ulyana's style and sets it on the sealed door, where sometimes, faintly, a voice answers. Emotional beat: memory as a living thing, tended like a garden.
